alias_map.why: One word covered four different situations: a file nobody had found, a file the connector could name, a file on local disk, and a file whose content had been read. A queue built on it cannot answer which units could be worked on this afternoon, which is the only question the queue exists to answer.

interpretation.old: SOURCE_READY on a K5 PL06 row
interpretation.because: the module DOCX is local and hash-verified and the unit's anchors resolve in it

interpretation.old: SOURCE_READY on a K5 PL01-PL08 candidate row
interpretation.because: the binary is readable but no frozen unit boundary exists for it

interpretation.new: SOURCE_LOCATED_BY_CONNECTOR, or SOURCE_CONTENT_READ where the PDF was actually read
interpretation.because: no K3 binary is on local disk; text came through the connector
the file is located and identified; it is the binary that is not local, and 'blocked' hid that distinction

retired_metric.why_retired: It counted a located K2 monolith and 30 unmapped K5 candidates as ready. It was arithmetically correct and practically meaningless.

excludes: units whose source is only located by a connector

anything whose binary is not readable in this environment
headline.note: A located record is not an executable unit. That distinction is the whole reason for the state list.

derivation: Every row and count is computed from artifacts on disk — the frozen boundary map, the extract and model files, the custody manifest and the inventory. No percentage is typed.
